claim: The hieroglyph for ’sun’ could also serve for ’day’ or as the name of the sun god Re.
fact_check_evidence: The sun-disk sign (Gardiner N5) is a logogram for sun and day and an ideogram for Ra. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_(hieroglyph))

claim: The house sign, also used for the sound pr, helped write the verb ’to go out’; an added sign of walking legs, a meaning sign called a determinative, marked the difference.

claim: Hieroglyphs were usually written from right to left, and the direction the signs faced showed which way to read.
fact_check_evidence: Asymmetrical signs such as people and animals face the start of the line, so their orientation gives the reading direction. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_hieroglyphs https://www.historyskills.com/classroom/year-7/year-7-hieroglyphs-reading/)

claim: Hieroglyphic writing apparently arose in the late predynastic period, just before Egypt’s First Dynasty.
fact_check_evidence: The earliest hieroglyphic inscriptions, such as labels from Abydos, date to the late predynastic period before the First Dynasty. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_hieroglyphs)

claim: The English word ’paper’ comes from papyrus, a reedy plant that grows along the Nile.
fact_check_evidence: Paper takes its name from papyrus, the writing material made from the Cyperus papyrus plant. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papyrus)

claim: The papyrus plant grew abundantly in marshes and was long cultivated in the Nile Delta.
fact_check_evidence: Papyrus grew in abundance in the Egyptian Delta and was widely cultivated there in ancient times. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyperus_papyrus https://www.worldhistory.org/Egyptian_Papyrus/)

claim: Besides writing material, papyrus was used to make rope, matting, sandals and boats.
fact_check_evidence: Egyptians used papyrus for reed boats, mats, rope, sandals and baskets. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyperus_papyrus https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reed_boat)

claim: A papyrus sheet was made from strips of the stem’s pith laid side by side, crossed at right angles by a second layer, dampened and pressed so the plant’s sap glued them, then hammered and dried in the sun.

claim: Papyrus sheets were pasted together into rolls, usually of no more than 20 sheets.
fact_check_evidence: Sheets were joined with paste into rolls; roughly 20 sheets was the usual length of a commercial roll. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papyrus)

fact_check_evidence: Single stroke for 1, cattle hobble for 10, coil of rope for 100, water lily or lotus for 1,000. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_numerals)

claim: Problems in the Rhind papyrus include sharing bread and beer as wages and measuring the areas of fields.

fact_check_evidence: The 2023 study characterized a corridor about 9 m long near the north face; an endoscope confirmed it. (https://www.livescience.com/cosmic-rays-reveal-hidden-30-foot-long-corridor-in-egypts-great-pyramid https://www.sciencenews.org/article/muon-particle-egypt-great-pyramid-void)

claim: Amenhotep I’s mummy, so finely wrapped with garlands and a mask that it was never opened in modern times, was digitally unwrapped with CT scans in 2021 by Sahar Saleem and Zahi Hawass.
fact_check_evidence: NPR and others report the 2021 Frontiers in Medicine study led by Cairo University radiologist Sahar Saleem with Zahi Hawass. (https://www.npr.org/2021/12/30/1069027478/the-mummy-of-an-egyptian-pharaoh-has-been-digitally-unwrapped https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/12/28/egypt-digitally-unwraps-mummy-of-famed-pharaoh)

claim: The CT scans showed Amenhotep I was about 35 when he died, had good teeth and was buried with 30 amulets inside his wrappings.
fact_check_evidence: Reports of the study: about 35 years old at death, good teeth, 30 amulets and a gold girdle. (https://www.npr.org/2021/12/30/1069027478/the-mummy-of-an-egyptian-pharaoh-has-been-digitally-unwrapped https://www.upi.com/Science_News/2021/12/28/Egypt-mummy-AmenhotepI-CT-scan/2091640716807/)

claim: Sarah Parcak of the University of Alabama at Birmingham processes satellite images to see in infrared, invisible to the human eye; in the desert they show moisture differences above buried mud bricks.
fact_check_evidence: Parcak’s method enhances infrared satellite data to detect subtle surface changes caused by mud brick buried underground. (https://www.nationalgeographic.com/magazine/article/satellite-archaeology https://encyclopediaofalabama.org/article/sarah-parcak/)

claim: Parcak’s team mapped the street grid of Tanis, once a capital in the Nile Delta, and tracked tomb looting after 2011.
fact_check_evidence: Satellite work revealed a detailed street plan of Tanis, a Delta capital, and a looting map after the 2011 unrest. (https://www.nationalgeographic.com/magazine/article/satellite-archaeology https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Parcak)

claim: In 2022, Zahi Hawass, Egypt’s former antiquities minister, launched a petition for the Rosetta Stone’s return that passed 100,000 signatures.
fact_check_evidence: News reports in 2022: Hawass’s petition to return the Rosetta Stone gathered more than 100,000 signatures. (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-11-30/egyptians-call-on-british-museum-to-return-rosetta-stone/101719316 https://www.thenationalnews.com/world/2022/11/21/petition-to-return-rosetta-stone-to-egypt-seeks-a-million-signatures/)

claim: Hawass also calls for the return of the bust of Nefertiti from Berlin and the Dendera Zodiac from the Louvre, saying these unique objects belong in Egypt.
fact_check_evidence: Hawass has campaigned for the Rosetta Stone, the Nefertiti bust and the Dendera Zodiac to return to Egypt. (https://www.deseret.com/u-s-world/2022/8/23/23318143/zahi-hawass-calls-on-british-museum-to-return-rosetta-stone/ https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/9/8/egyptian-archaeologist-urges-german-museum-to-return-nefertitis-bust)

claim: Hawass argues that the bust of Nefertiti, found in 1912 and taken to Berlin in 1913, left Egypt illegally.
fact_check_evidence: In his 2024 petition Hawass said all the evidence shows the bust left Egypt illegally. (https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/nefertiti-bust-return-egypt-petition-berlin-museum-rcna170171 https://www.jpost.com/archaeology/archaeology-around-the-world/article-826421)

claim: The British Museum says the Rosetta Stone came to Britain under an 1801 treaty signed by a representative of Egypt, notes that Egypt’s government has made no formal request, and that 21 of the 28 known copies of the decree are in Egypt.
fact_check_evidence: AP reporting quoted the museum: the 1801 treaty includes the signature of a representative of Egypt, and no formal return request has been made. (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-11-30/egyptians-call-on-british-museum-to-return-rosetta-stone/101719316 https://www.thenationalnews.com/world/2022/11/21/petition-to-return-rosetta-stone-to-egypt-seeks-a-million-signatures/)

claim: Berlin’s museum points out that the Nefertiti bust left Egypt through an official division of finds in 1913, overseen by an inspector of Egypt’s antiquities service.
fact_check_evidence: The Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation says the bust came to Berlin legally through a division of finds from an authorized excavation. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nefertiti_Bust https://www.newarab.com/features/inside-egypts-bid-return-nefertitis-bust-berlin-museum)

claim: The Grand Egyptian Museum, near the Great Pyramid at Giza, officially opened on 1 November 2025 with about 100,000 artifacts.
fact_check_evidence: Reports of the opening: the GEM on the Giza Plateau was inaugurated on 1 November 2025 and holds about 100,000 artifacts. (https://www.deseret.com/entertainment/2025/11/04/grand-egyptian-museum-opening/ https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Egyptian_Museum)

claim: At the Grand Egyptian Museum, Tutankhamun’s entire collection is shown together for the first time since its discovery.
fact_check_evidence: The Tutankhamun galleries display the complete collection from the tomb together for the first time since 1922. (https://www.deseret.com/entertainment/2025/11/04/grand-egyptian-museum-opening/ https://allafrica.com/stories/202509220038.html)

claim: Howard Carter, who opened Tutankhamun’s tomb in 1922, lived until 1939.
fact_check_evidence: Carter died in London on 2 March 1939, about 16 years after opening the tomb, which undercuts the curse legend. (https://www.historytoday.com/archive/months-past/tutankhamuns-curse https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Carter)

claim: The idea that slaves built the pyramids comes from the Greek historian Herodotus, misreadings of the biblical book of Exodus and Hollywood films.
fact_check_evidence: Summaries of the debate trace the slave-builder picture to Herodotus, Exodus and films; archaeology points to paid labor. (https://www.britannica.com/place/What-evidence-suggests-that-the-builders-of-the-Great-Pyramid-of-Giza-were-paid-laborers-rather-than-enslaved-people https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giza_pyramid_complex)

claim: Near the Giza pyramids, archaeologists found workers’ districts with bakeries and workshops, and workers’ tombs close to the pyramids, some naming the dead; most now think paid laborers built them.
fact_check_evidence: Excavations at Giza found the workers’ town and cemetery; most archaeologists conclude the builders were paid Egyptian laborers. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giza_pyramid_complex https://www.britannica.com/video/did-enslaved-people-build-the-pyramids/-259236)

claim: Near the Giza pyramids, archaeologists found workers’ districts with bakeries and workshops, and workers’ tombs close to the pyramids, some naming the dead; most now think paid laborers built them.
fact_check_evidence: Excavations at Giza found the workers’ town and cemetery; most archaeologists conclude the builders were paid Egyptian laborers. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giza_pyramid_complex https://www.britannica.com/video/did-enslaved-people-build-the-pyramids/-259236)

claim: In 2013, archaeologists at Wadi al-Jarf on the Red Sea found the oldest known inscribed papyri, including the logbook of an official named Merer.
fact_check_evidence: The Wadi al-Jarf papyri, excavated in 2013 by Pierre Tallet’s team, are the oldest inscribed papyri known and include Merer’s diary. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diary_of_Merer https://archaeology.org/issues/july-august-2022/features/egypt-wadi-el-jarf-port-papyri/)

claim: Merer’s logbook records his crew shipping limestone by boat from the Tura quarries to Giza for Khufu’s pyramid, in half-day entries.
fact_check_evidence: The diary documents transporting white limestone blocks from Tura to Giza for Khufu’s pyramid, logged in half-day increments. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diary_of_Merer https://www.nationalgeographic.com/premium/article/red-sea-scrolls-pyramids-egypt)

claim: Cleopatra belonged to a Macedonian Greek dynasty, but her mother’s identity is uncertain, and her coins and portrait busts do not all agree.
fact_check_evidence: Britannica: daughter of Ptolemy XII and most likely Cleopatra V; the portraits on coins and busts differ. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleopatra https://www.britannica.com/biography/Cleopatra-queen-of-Egypt)

claim: Plutarch wrote that Cleopatra’s beauty was “not altogether incomparable,” but that conversation with her had “an irresistible charm.”
fact_check_evidence: Plutarch, Life of Antony 27, in the Perrin translation: her beauty was not altogether incomparable, but converse with her had an irresistible charm. (https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Plut.+Ant.+27 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleopatra)

claim: In 46 BCE Julius Caesar reformed Rome’s calendar by adopting the Egyptian solar calendar, advised by Sosigenes of Alexandria: 365 and a quarter days, with an extra day every fourth year.
fact_check_evidence: The Julian calendar, introduced in 46 BCE on the advice of Sosigenes, was modeled on the Egyptian solar year with a leap day every four years. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_calendar https://www.britannica.com/topic/calendar/The-Julian-calendar)

claim: Pope Gregory XIII fine-tuned Caesar’s calendar in 1582, and the Gregorian calendar gradually replaced the Julian one.
fact_check_evidence: The Gregorian reform of 1582 corrected the Julian calendar’s drift and gradually replaced it. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorian_calendar https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_calendar)

claim: The letter A goes back to a sign shaped like an ox’s head: early Semitic writing in Sinai adopted it around 1500 BCE, the Phoenicians called it aleph (“ox”), and the Greeks renamed it alpha and used it for a vowel.
fact_check_evidence: Aleph derives from an ox-head pictogram in Proto-Sinaitic, influenced by an Egyptian hieroglyph; the Greeks turned it into the vowel alpha, and Latin A followed. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleph https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A)

claim: The inventors of the alphabet were influenced by Egyptian writing; inscriptions from Sinai show a stage between Egyptian hieroglyphs and the Semitic alphabet.
fact_check_evidence: The Proto-Sinaitic script, from Egyptian turquoise mines in Sinai, is generally believed to have evolved from Egyptian hieroglyphs. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proto-Sinaitic_script https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphabet)

claim: The word “paper” comes from papyrus, the Egyptian writing material, which the Greeks adopted and the Roman Empire used widely.
fact_check_evidence: Dictionaries trace English paper, via Latin papyrus, to Greek papyros, the Egyptian reed writing material. (https://www.etymonline.com/word/paper https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papyrus)

claim: Books and documents on papyrus were still made, sporadically, until about the 12th century.
fact_check_evidence: Papyrus remained in use in Europe and Egypt into the medieval period, with the latest uses around the 11th and 12th centuries. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papyrus https://www.etymonline.com/word/paper)
